description:
pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:237-306 — parse_rfc3339_to_unix_ms() is ~70 lines of hand-rolled parsing using Howard Hinnant's days-from-civil algorithm. Refuses to pull in chrono, time, or jiff just to convert 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fff]Z' to ms-since-epoch.

The Google log_list.json schema documents the timestamp format precisely; it doesn't need a general-purpose datetime parser. The hand-roll is:
- Bounded scope (one format)
- Documented (cites Howard Hinnant by URL)
- Independent tests with python datetime as oracle (schema_tests at lines 308-342)
- Allocates zero
- ~70 lines including tests

chrono / time / jiff are each ~50-300KB of compiled code, have their own MSRV concerns, and pull in additional deps. For one timestamp format, the hand-roll is correct.

A future contributor might suggest 'use chrono, this is reinventing the wheel.' Workspace dependency policy (and pre-launch 'design closure' framing) supports rejecting that suggestion. The wheel here is one circle, the chrono wheel is a clock tower.
title: Hand-rolled RFC 3339 parser refuses to take a dep on chrono just for ts→ms conversion
